/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Grounding
  Which assignments of tracks to binders exist over a trace, how a broken track is followed, and
  the per-grounding timeline of verdicts.

  A track is a source's identity, not an object's. When a tracker breaks and the adapter claims a
  continuation (`Scene.links`, old ↦ new), the trace is rewritten once to canonical identities
  when the break is shorter than the manifest's re-identification gap; the instants inside the gap
  are unknown (identityGap), never a fresh party. A binder whose track is not present at an
  instant outside any gap leaves the rule not engaged there: the other party has left the scene.

  Groundings are tuples of distinct candidates that are co-present at some instant; each
  grounding evaluates the rule once over the whole trace, and formulas that depend on a subset of
  the binders are shared across the groundings that agree on that subset.

  Rules never import this file: a rule that could see the census of tracks could special-case it.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.RuleEval
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Grounding
open Semantics

/-- An assignment of canonical tracks to binder names, and of regions to the variables a
    concept's instance takes as region formals (a rule's groundings bind none). -/
structure Grounding where
  assign : List (String × TrackId)
  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

def Grounding.render (g : Grounding) : String :=
  String.intercalate "," (g.assign.map fun (n, t) => s!"{n}={t}")
def Grounding.binding (g : Grounding) : Binding :=
  ⟨g.assign.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Val.track t)) ++ g.regions.map fun (n, r) => (n, Val.region r)⟩

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Identity: canonical tracks through accepted links, applied to the trace once
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- The scene with every track id replaced by its canonical identity. -/
def canonicalScene (cm : List (TrackId × TrackId)) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
  let c := canon cm
  { s with
    subject := s.subject.map c
    users := s.users.map fun u => { u with track := c u.track }
    occupancyObserved := s.occupancyObserved.map c
    occupies := s.occupies.map fun (t, r) => (c t, r)
    relations := s.relations.map fun m => { m with a := c m.a, b := c m.b }
    intents := s.intents.map fun d => { d with vehicle := c d.vehicle } }

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Setup: the canonical, indexed trace and the rule set
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
structure Setup where
  rules : List Rule
  d : Primitives.Ctx
  gap : Q
  cm : List (TrackId × TrackId) := []

def Setup.mk' (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Setup :=
  let arr := τ.toArray
  let cm := canonMap arr gap
  { rules := rules, d := Primitives.Ctx.mk' (τ.map (canonicalScene cm)) ρ, gap := gap, cm := cm }

/-- The setup of a trace every evaluation reaches: built only when `Admission.defects` finds no
    defect in the trace as written, else the defects. -/
def Setup.admit (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Except (List String) Setup :=
  match Admission.defects τ gap with
  | [] => .ok (Setup.mk' rules τ ρ gap)
  | ds => .error ds

def Setup.n (S : Setup) : Nat := S.d.n
def Setup.scenes (S : Setup) : Array Scene := S.d.scenes
def Setup.ctx (S : Setup) (β : Binding) : SemCtx := Rule.context S.rules S.d β
def Setup.tracks (S : Setup) : List TrackId := (S.scenes.toList.flatMap (·.tracks)).eraseDups
/-- First and last instant at which a canonical identity is present. -/
def Setup.span (S : Setup) (t : TrackId) : Option (Nat × Nat) :=
  match firstSeen S.scenes t, lastSeen S.scenes t with
  | some a, some b => some (a, b)
  | _, _ => none

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Enumeration
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- Tracks that satisfy a binder's class at some instant (evaluated once per track). -/
def candidates (S : Setup) (b : Binder) : List TrackId :=
  S.tracks.filter fun t =>
    (Rule.evalRuleFormula (S.ctx ⟨[(b.name, .track t)]⟩) b.cls).any fun r => r.v == .t

def spansOverlap (S : Setup) (a b : TrackId) : Bool :=
  match S.span a, S.span b with
  | some (a0, a1), some (b0, b1) => a0 ≤ b1 && b0 ≤ a1
  | _, _ => false

/-- All assignments of distinct, pairwise co-present candidates to the binders, subject first.
    Each binder's candidates are computed once. -/
def groundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List Grounding :=
  let cands := r.binders.map fun b => (b.name, candidates S b)
  let rec go (bs : List (String × List TrackId)) (used : List TrackId) : List (List (String × TrackId)) :=
    match bs with
    | [] => [[]]
    | (name, cs) :: rest =>
      cs.filter (fun c => !used.contains c && used.all (spansOverlap S c)) |>.flatMap fun c =>
        (go rest (c :: used)).map fun tail => (name, c) :: tail
  (go cands []).map fun a => { assign := a }

/-- Predicted grounding count without enumerating: the product of candidate counts (an upper
    bound when candidates overlap). -/
def predictedGroundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Nat :=
  r.binders.foldl (fun acc b => acc * (candidates S b).length) 1

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Timelines
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- One evaluation of a rule for a grounding: the verdict per instant, whether the rule was
    engaged at some instant with every party present, and whether every party was present at
    some instant at all. -/
structure Timeline where
  verdicts : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)
  live : Bool
  present : Bool
  deriving Repr

/-- Evaluate a rule for a grounding once. A binder absent inside its identity's span is an
    identity gap (unknown); absent outside it, the rule is not engaged. -/
def evaluate (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Timeline :=
  let c := S.ctx g.binding
  let engaged := r.engagedAll c
  let obl := Rule.evalRuleFormula c r.obligation
  let spans := g.assign.map fun (_, t) => (t, S.span t)
  let rows := (Array.range S.n).map fun i =>
    let s := S.scenes[i]!
    let missing := spans.filter fun (t, _) => !s.tracks.contains t
    let v : Verdict :=
      if missing.isEmpty then verdictAt engaged[i]! obl[i]!
      else
        let inGap := missing.filter fun (_, sp) => match sp with
          | some (a, b) => a < i && i < b
          | none => false
        if inGap.isEmpty then .notApplicable
        else .unknown (inGap.map fun (t, _) => .identityGap t)
    (s.t, v, missing.isEmpty && engaged[i]!.v == .t, missing.isEmpty)
  ⟨rows.map fun (t, v, _, _) => (t, v), rows.any fun (_, _, l, _) => l, rows.any fun (_, _, _, p) => p⟩

def timeline (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Array (Timestamp × Verdict) := (evaluate S r g).verdicts

/-- The verdict of a grounding at one instant. -/
def verdictAt (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) (i : Nat) : Verdict :=
  ((timeline S r g)[i]?).map (·.2) |>.getD (.unknown [.outOfRange])

/-- The episode verdict: a violation anywhere is a violation; else any unknown is unknown (with
    every reason); else engaged anywhere is compliant; else not applicable. -/
def episode (tl : List Verdict) : Verdict :=
  if tl.any (· == .violated) then .violated
  else
    let unknowns := tl.flatMap Verdict.reasons
    if tl.any (fun v => match v with | .unknown _ => true | _ => false) then .unknown unknowns.eraseDups
    else if tl.any (· == .compliant) then .compliant
    else .notApplicable

/-- Every grounding evaluated once: its episode verdict and timeline. -/
def check (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List (Grounding × Timeline × Verdict) :=
  (groundings S r).map fun g =>
    let tl := evaluate S r g
    (g, tl, episode (tl.verdicts.toList.map (·.2)))

/-- Engaged (applicability true) at some instant for some grounding: the rule says something on
    this trace. -/
def live (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Bool := (check S r).any fun (_, tl, _) => tl.live

end Grounding
end TrafficSpec

1	/-
2	  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission
3	  What a trace must satisfy, as written, before any rule is evaluated on it: the declared facts
4	  (assumptions and intentions) name what their scene holds, each once, by well-formed ids; no
5	  structure is labelled with an abstract kind or lists one among the kinds its source cannot tell
6	  (an abstract kind is the union of the kinds refining it, read only by a formula); and the
7	  accepted re-identification links are one-to-one.
8	
9	  The checks are exact and read no geometry, so a recorded trace, a JSON case and a Lean witness
10	  are held to them alike. `Grounding.Setup.admit` calls them; every evaluation builds its setup
11	  there.
12	-/
13	import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Identity
14	import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Assumptions
15	import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Intentions
16	
17	namespace TrafficSpec
18	namespace Admission
19	
20	private def duplicates {α : Type} [BEq α] (xs : List α) : List α :=
21	  (xs.filter fun x => xs.count x > 1).eraseDups
22	
23	/-- The defects of one scene's declared facts. -/
24	def sceneDefects (s : Scene) : List String :=
25	  let at_ := s!"scene t={s.t}"
26	  (s.intents.flatMap fun d =>
27	    let who := s!"{at_}: intent record ({d.vehicle}, {d.target})"
28	    (if s.tracks.contains d.vehicle then [] else [s!"{who}: vehicle {d.vehicle} is not a road user of the scene"]) ++
29	    (if (s.structure? d.target).isSome then [] else [s!"{who}: target {d.target} is not a structure of the scene"]) ++
30	    ((duplicates (d.values.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` listed more than once") ++
31	    ((d.values.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!IntId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` is not a well-formed intention id")) ++
32	  ((duplicates (s.intents.map fun d => (d.vehicle, d.target))).map fun (v, r) => s!"{at_}: more than one intent record for ({v}, {r})") ++
33	  (s.structures.flatMap fun st =>
34	    (if st.kind.isAbstract then [s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} is labelled `{st.kind}`, an abstract kind; label it with a kind that refines `{st.kind}`"] else []) ++
35	    ((st.unobservedKinds.filter (·.isAbstract)).eraseDups.map fun k =>
36	      s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} lists `{k}` among unobserved_kinds, an abstract kind; list the kinds refining it that the source cannot tell")) ++
37	  ((duplicates (s.assumptions.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{at_}: assumption `{id}` listed more than once") ++
38	  ((s.assumptions.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!AsmId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{at_}: `{id}` is not a well-formed assumption id")
39	
40	/-- Accepted links that give a track two successors or two predecessors. -/
41	def linkDefects (τ : Array Scene) (gap : Q) : List String :=
42	  let links := Grounding.acceptedLinks τ gap
43	  ((duplicates (links.map (·.1))).map fun t =>
44	    s!"track {t} is continued by more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.1 == t)}") ++
45	  ((duplicates (links.map (·.2))).map fun t =>
46	    s!"track {t} continues more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.2 == t)}")
47	
48	/-- Every defect of the trace as written; empty for a trace every evaluation may read. -/
49	def defects (τ : Trace) (gap : Q) : List String :=
50	  τ.flatMap sceneDefects ++ linkDefects τ.toArray gap
51	
52	end Admission
53	end TrafficSpec

  are held to them alike. `Grounding.Setup.admit` calls them; every evaluation builds its setup
  there.

import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Identity
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Assumptions
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Intentions

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Admission

private def duplicates {α : Type} [BEq α] (xs : List α) : List α :=
  (xs.filter fun x => xs.count x > 1).eraseDups

/-- The defects of one scene's declared facts. -/
def sceneDefects (s : Scene) : List String :=
  let at_ := s!"scene t={s.t}"
  (s.intents.flatMap fun d =>
    let who := s!"{at_}: intent record ({d.vehicle}, {d.target})"
    (if s.tracks.contains d.vehicle then [] else [s!"{who}: vehicle {d.vehicle} is not a road user of the scene"]) ++
    (if (s.structure? d.target).isSome then [] else [s!"{who}: target {d.target} is not a structure of the scene"]) ++
    ((duplicates (d.values.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` listed more than once") ++
    ((d.values.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!IntId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` is not a well-formed intention id")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.intents.map fun d => (d.vehicle, d.target))).map fun (v, r) => s!"{at_}: more than one intent record for ({v}, {r})") ++
  (s.structures.flatMap fun st =>
    (if st.kind.isAbstract then [s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} is labelled `{st.kind}`, an abstract kind; label it with a kind that refines `{st.kind}`"] else []) ++
    ((st.unobservedKinds.filter (·.isAbstract)).eraseDups.map fun k =>
      s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} lists `{k}` among unobserved_kinds, an abstract kind; list the kinds refining it that the source cannot tell")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.assumptions.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{at_}: assumption `{id}` listed more than once") ++
  ((s.assumptions.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!AsmId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{at_}: `{id}` is not a well-formed assumption id")

/-- Accepted links that give a track two successors or two predecessors. -/
def linkDefects (τ : Array Scene) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  let links := Grounding.acceptedLinks τ gap
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.1))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} is continued by more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.1 == t)}") ++
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.2))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} continues more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.2 == t)}")

/-- Every defect of the trace as written; empty for a trace every evaluation may read. -/
def defects (τ : Trace) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  τ.flatMap sceneDefects ++ linkDefects τ.toArray gap

end Admission
end TrafficSpec

    Build.north (enters := some 10)

  Build.lane 12 [(cm (-350), cm 350), (cm 0, cm 350), (cm 0, cm 20000), (cm (-350), cm 20000)]
    Build.south (enters := some 10)

# NRS_484B_253_o1 — coding session result

**Final verdict: `OK`** (11 witnesses, 12 names, composes nothing, 3 coder narrowings).

## The two files

- `library/TrafficSpec/Rules/NRS_484B/NRS_484B_253_o1.lean` — binder class, applicability,
  obligation, and three declared narrowings on `ob1`.
- `library/TrafficSpecWitness/NRS_484B/NRS_484B_253_o1.lean` — the four planned scenes, the two
  planned branches, and five branch witnesses of my own (`branch_3` … `branch_7`).

How each span is written (the header of the rule file carries the same, per span):

- `s1` → `ru_aggregate v "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"` as the binder's class, one atom, never the
  classes it covers.
- `t1` → `existsRegion "intersection" "j" (rel_occupies v j ∧ …)`; the junction is the subject's own
  by occupancy, and the same whole selection (occupancy **and** the declared intention) is written
  again in the obligation under `forallRegion "intersection" "j"`, since the duty is owed at every
  junction so selected and a region bound in one formula is not in scope in the other.
- `c1` → `intent "int.left_turn" v j`, read at the judged observation (no future operator over it).
- `ob1` → `forallUser "u"` with the subject excluded by `same`; `u` of the aggregate; "approaching
  from the opposite direction" through the carriers (`rel_occupies`, `st_lane_enters` on a
  `travel_region`, and the normalised dot product of the two carriers' `st_lane_direction` at or
  below `−p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance`); "within the intersection" as `rel_occupies u j`;
  granting precedence as no `rel_contact` and no loss of clearance.
- `st1` → `st_region_geometry_distance u j ≤ kin_speed u × p.yield_headway_time` (a product, never a
  ratio) or the clearance lost within `p.yield_conflict_horizon`.

## Gate runs

1. **`WITNESS_FAIL`** — (a) `blind` was unknown for `absent_atom:st_lane_enters` as well as for the
   masked `st.lane_direction`: the carrier quantifier ranges over `travel_region`, which covers the
   intersection, and `st_lane_enters` is unrecorded (unknown, not false) on the junction region
   itself, so that unknown leaked into the verdict's reasons. (b) `branch_3` built the junction
   without an outline, which the adapter cannot produce ("where occupancy is observed every
   structure needs one").
   *Changed:* excluded the junction from being its own approach carrier (`¬ same cu j`,
   `¬ same cs j`), declared as narrowing 3; rebuilt `branch_3` as a van whose body and lane are
   observed but whose speed and velocity are not.
2. **`VACUOUS`** — obligation leaf 9, the headway comparison, moved no decided witness: in
   `branch_1` the clearance limb was true as well, and in `branch_2` making it true left the duty
   discharged. *Changed:* added `branch_7`, the one shape in which that limb alone decides — a
   truck waiting mid-turn, an oncoming van 2.3 m short of the junction at 2 m/s (bound 3.0 m) that
   is **not** within the junction and whose centre approach falls past the horizon (9 m at 2 m/s),
   clipping the truck's nose, so precedence is denied by contact while the headway limb alone makes
   it owed.
3. **`OK`**.

## Choices the node left open (all declared as narrowings, kind `reading`, on `ob1`)

1. **What "its closest approach" is measured by.** The record names `prim.closest_approach_within`,
   `prim.closest_approach_distance` *and* `rel.surface_gap` for one clearance. Written as: the
   centres approach within `p.yield_conflict_horizon`, and at that approach either the centre
   distance or the gap between the nearest points of the two bodies lies below
   `p.yield_min_clearance`. The `within` primitive gates both, so two bodies already drawing apart
   are not read as a failure to grant precedence (contact is read beside it on its own atom), and
   the undefined value the distance primitive carries where no approach occurs never reaches a
   verdict. `branch_6` is the witness in which the nearest-point limb alone decides and `branch_5`
   the one in which contact alone does.
2. **The subject's approach carrier is existential** — some carrier it occupies whose entrance end
   is that junction. The ontology fixes a road user's approach by occupancy and entrance topology,
   and the words single no further one out.
3. **The junction is not its own approach carrier.** `st.travel_region`, the kind the record names,
   covers the intersection, but `st.lane_enters` is the source's record of an approach segment and
   is never recorded on the junction it enters ("A carrier enters one carrier … one intersection at
   most"), so on the junction region that relation is unknown rather than false. Excluding it
   removes no case the relation could decide and no vehicle the duty could reach; keeping it in only
   put a spurious unknown into every verdict (which is what run 1 showed on `blind`).

Other writing decisions that follow the record's words and are therefore not narrowings: `le` for
"at most its speed times p.yield_headway_time" and `lt` for "below p.yield_min_clearance"; the
standard's two limbs joined by `or`, as the record's obligation states; `forallRegion` over the
selected junctions, since the record requires the duty at each.

## Witnesses

| name | verdict | what it exercises |
|---|---|---|
| `forbid` | violated | van within the junction on the opposing approach, bodies touching |
| `permit` | compliant | subject alone in the scene; nothing owed precedence |
| `idle` | not applicable | the declared plan at that junction is **not** a left turn (decided false) |
| `blind` | unknown | `st.lane_direction` masked: opposition unknown, contact denies precedence, verdict unknown for that atom only |
| `branch_1` | violated | van 15 m out at 12 m/s (bound 18 m) and a 0.52 m centre approach within the horizon |
| `branch_2` | compliant | van 150 m out at 10 m/s; neither limb of the standard, duty discharged |
| `branch_3` | violated | van's speed and velocity unobserved: only "within the intersection" makes it owed |
| `branch_4` | violated | van 21.5 m out (bound 18 m), so owed by the clearance limb alone (0.02 m approach) |
| `branch_5` | violated | both at rest and touching: no centre approach within the horizon, contact alone |
| `branch_6` | violated | centres never closer than 2.55 m, bodies 0.5 m apart: the nearest-point limb |
| `branch_7` | violated | the headway limb alone makes the van owed (see run 2) |

Geometry (one map for all scenes): a 7 m × 7 m junction (region 10), the subject's northbound
approach lane (region 11) and the opposing southbound approach lane (region 12), their designated
directions exactly opposed. Occupancy is stated in every scene, since each body lies across two
regions and a reference point lies in one. Nothing Core computes is supplied: the surface gap, the
contact and the closest approach all come from the positions, headings, extents and velocities.

## Why I finished

The gate returned `OK` on run 3 of a budget of 6: every declaration matches the node, every claimed
atom, primitive and parameter is used and used as its contract states, every quantified variable is
anchored to the binder by `rel_occupies`, all eleven witnesses reach their planned verdicts (the
`unknown` one for the masked atom only), and no leaf is idle. The node needed no repair: every span
it carries could be written with the atoms it claims.
